content:
Cabinet
received a report of the Housing Strategy, Policy and Projects
Manager that set out changes to the council’s nomination to a
Board member from May 2026.
 
The
Mayor invited Councillor Pattinson to introduce the report and
noted that, as she had mentioned at the beginning of the meeting,
she would not be voting on it.
 
Councillor Pattinson introduced the report.  She explained that the under the current rules the
council was able to nominate a Board member.  The report explained that the rationale had
changed.  Currently there were
negotiations taking place to merge Watford Community Housing with
Thrive Homes.  Councillor Pattinson
advised that currently she was the council-appointed representative
to the Board.  She was content to step
down as proposed in the report.  She
agreed with the principle of removing the Board nomination
as long as members were satisfied that
there was a strong governance process in place and residents had a
voice.  The proposal was instead to
appoint a Cabinet member to the Customer Experience
Committee.  This committee covered
everything related to customers, including complaints, nominations
and any customer experiences.  She
welcomed Watford Community Housing’s commitment to a gateway
organisation.  She supported the
recommendations and the way forward.
 
The
Mayor thanked Councillor Pattinson for the presentation.
 
Councillor Williams noted the proposal from Watford to be able
to nominate a Cabinet member to the Customer Experience
Committee.  He asked whether the same
offer would be made to Three Rivers if the merger with Thrive went
ahead.
 
The
Mayor commented that this was not a given at this time.  Councillor Pattinson added that this not yet known
as the merger decision had not been finalised.
 
The
Mayor noted that the geography covered by both organisations since
they were set up had changed. 
 
Councillor Stotesbury recognised that the Customer Experience
Committee covered many things, including rent reviews and
scrutinising the gateway.  The trust
covered areas outside of Watford, for example Hendon.
 
Councillor Bell said that residents asked him what was
happening.  Previously it had been
Watford Borough Council’s housing stock.  It was important the council would still be able
to scrutinise the organisation.
 
The
Mayor referred to the third recommendation which mentioned the
continued engagement with the council and after local government
reorganisation had taken place. 
 
Resolved –
 

1.         that Watford
Borough Council nominates a Cabinet Member to form part of the
Customer Experience Committee through the usual process of
appointing representatives to outside bodies at Council to be
confirmed at the next Annual Council in May.

 

2.         that
Watford Borough Council writes to Watford Community Housing to
confirm it will no longer be seeking to appoint a Board Member. The
current Board Member will step down after the Annual Council
meeting in May. This letter shall include the commitment below as
the basis for that decision.
 

3.         that Cabinet
notes the commitment from Watford Community Housing
that:
 

1.   Watford Borough
Council will nominate a Cabinet Member to form part of the Customer
Experience Committee.

2.   That Watford
Community Housing commit to continuing to operate as a Gateway
Organisation empowering a strong Gateway Membership team that will
include tenant representation from Watford in any future
organisation.

3.   That Watford
Community Housing will continue to engage, via the Executive team,
with Senior Officers and Members from the council, to develop and
align strategic opportunities and delivery within Watford. This
engagement will include the exchange of performance information,
consultation on strategic direction and active support to ensure
ongoing strong engagement after local government
reorganisation.

content:
Cabinet
received a report of the Chief Finance Officer which set out the
draft budget for 2026/27 and the Medium
Term Financial Strategy to 2028/29.  The report would be further considered at Council
on 27 January 2026.
 
The
Mayor invited Councillor Begum to introduce the report.
 
Councillor Begum explained the content of the report, which
included the draft budget for 2026/27, the Medium Term Financial Strategy, the Capital
programme and, the Capital Strategy 2026/27, including the Treasury
Management Strategy, prudential indicators and Minimum Revenue
Provision Policy, and advice from the Chief Finance Officer
regarding general reserves and balances and planning
horizon. 
 
Councillor Begum advised that the Fair Funding Review draft
proposals had been announced on 17 December with the final figures
laid before the House of Commons at the end of January beginning of
February.
 
Councillor Begum stated that the administration wanted to put
the community and residents first.  It
was proposed to freeze Council Tax for the forthcoming
year.  She outlined some of the
proposals, which included expanding the Environmental Protection
team and additional litter picking on high
speed roads.
 
Councillor Begum welcomed the feedback from Finance Scrutiny
Committee and members’ positive affirmation of the
proposals.  There had been a
recommendation to place the identified funding for Local Government
Reform into a reserve.  This proposal
would be included in the report to Council.
 
The
Mayor thanked Councillor Begum and he
recognised the huge amount of work that gone into preparing the
budget.  He opened it up to comments and
questions from members.
 
Councillor Bell noted the comments about the Fair Funding Review
and that it appeared that all districts had done well with
additional funding over three years.  He
was pleased with this.
 
The
Mayor said that this could not be disputed and he welcomed the
multi-year funding.  However, he added
that the county funding had been cut.
 
Councillor Saffery said that many councils who benefited from
the Fair Funding Review would need to plug holes in their budgets
with the additional funding.  However,
Watford had acted with responsible stewardship over previous years
and would be able to do things to benefit its residents.
 
The
Mayor commented that the council’s administration had to
decide how to prioritise its funding. 
There were still many families struggling with the cost of living,
and to freeze Watford’s share of Council Tax whilst still
tackling key things were really
important.  He invited Councillor
Khan to speak.
 
Councillor Khan said the scrutiny committee had welcomed the
clarity that the Chief Finance Officer and her team had presented
the information.   It had been made
very clear about growth items and any reductions.  A key point discussed was government funding and
the extra £6.3 million over three years.  The scrutiny committee had discussed that the
Watford portion of Council Tax was recommended to be frozen, those
for Hertfordshire County Council and the Police and Crime
Commissioner were to be increased.  The
scrutiny committee had monitored Temporary Accommodation as a
priority.  The scrutiny committee was
able to help officers focus on this area.  The members had welcomed the provision of the
extra Temporary Accommodation reserve. 
This was an area that previously had not kept to its
budget.  The income assumptions had been
prudent. The scrutiny committee welcomed the strengthening of the
general reserves.  It had been
recommended that the funds set aside for Local Government Reform
should be transferred to reserves and then drawn down as
required.
 
The
Mayor thanked Councillor Khan for his feedback from the scrutiny
committee.  He confirmed that he was
happy with the recommendation to transfer the Local Government
Reform funding to reserves.
 
Councillor Begum thanked Councillors Khan and Bell and the other
scrutiny members for their great feedback to Cabinet.  In addition, she wished to thank the Chief Finance
Officer as this would be her last presentation to
Cabinet.
 
The
Mayor reminded members that it was necessary to have a recorded
vote for the budget.
 
In
accordance with the Local Authorities (Standing Orders) (England)
(Amendment) Regulations 2014 the votes were recorded as follows
–
 

Those in favour 

 
Mayor
Taylor, Councillors Begum, Hill, Pattinson, G Saffery, Stotesbury
and Williams
 
There
were no votes against or abstentions. 
The recommendations as set out in the report were CARRIED by 7
votes to 0.
 
Resolved –
 

1.         that the Chief
Finance Officer in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Finance is delegated the ability to amend the budget figures in
accordance with decisions taken at the Cabinet meeting on 19
January 2026 and any minor variations that may occur before the
Council meeting on 27 January 2026.

 

2.         that the
allocation of Strategic Community Infrastructure Levy to projects
over the medium term, as set out in Appendix 6 of Attachment 1
– Budget Planning Report, and incorporated into proposed
budgets is approved.

 

3.         that the
recommendations included in the Financial Monitoring Report 2025/26
– Quarter 2 are noted. Budget adjustments have been
incorporated into the proposed budget and capital investment
programme
 
Cabinet
recommends to Council
 

4.         that Council
resolves in accordance with the Local Authorities (Calculation of
Tax Base) Regulations 1992, the amount calculated by Watford
Borough Council as its Council Tax Base for the year 2026/27 is
35,687.7 as outlined in the report.

 

5.         that Council
approves the budget (Attachment 1) as laid out in the report,
including:

·      
the revenue budget for 2026/27

·      
the Capital Investment Programme 2025/26 to
2028/29.

           
This reflects budget adjustments and virements incorporated in the
Financial Monitoring Report 2025/26 – Quarter 1 and Quarter
2.

 

6.         that Council
approves the Capital Strategy for 2026/27, and delegates to the
Chief Finance Officer in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Finance responsibility for agreeing and maintaining the Treasury
Management Strategy Statement. (Attachment 2).

 

7.         that Council
agrees to freeze the annual Council Tax at 2025/26 level for a Band
D property in 2026/27. This will apply to all other
bands.

 

8.         that Council
notes the key risks identified and approves their proposed
mitigations as set out in Appendix 9 to Attachment 1 – Budget
Setting Report.
 

9.         that
Council notes the advice provided by the Chief Finance Officer on
the robustness of estimates and the adequacy of reserves as set out
in Appendix 8 to Attachment 1 – Budget Setting
Report.

 

10.       that Council notes the
indicative budgets for 2027/28 and 2028/29 as set out in Attachment
1 and Attachment 2.

 

11.       that the Chief Finance
Officer has delegated authority to vire
funds, realigning expenditure and income across budgets within the
budget envelope.

setting out the application which requested variations to
conditions 2 (approved plans), Condition 11 (A41 Toucan to the
Hempstead Road underpass) of planning permission 22/00322/FULM and
23/01023/VARM.  A duplicate application
had been submitted to Three Rivers District Council. 
 
The
Development Management Lead introduced the report.  She informed the committee that there had been an
amendment to sections 1.2 and 9.2 which updated the post title of
the officer delegated to grant the application if the Secretary of
State did not call in the application.
 
There
were no question from the committee for
the officer.  The Chair invited David
Bisoni to speak to the committee on behalf of the
applicant.
 
Mr
Bisoni introduced himself to the
committee.  He described Warner Bros.
Leavesden and its role it played in the film and television sector
and in the local community, providing local
residents with an entry into the industry.
 
Mr
Bisoni then explained the reasons for
the application to vary the conditions set out in the original
applications.  He advised that some of
the elements of the original application were in progress and
expected to open in March.  He detailed
the reasons for the change to the toucan crossing, explaining that
the previously approved site would now clash with access to the new
Lidl building being constructed on the A41.  He noted that there were no objections from
statutory consultees.

the original application, only the requested
variations.

the application was required to come to committee as it related to
a major application.

crossing was much better.

content:
The
committee received a report of the Principal Planning Officer which
set out the request for variations to conditions 1 (approved
drawings) and 27 (Part M compliance) for variation of Condition 1
attached to planning permission 22/01481/VARM dated 27 September
2023 and for variation of Condition 2 (revisions of approved plans)
of planning permission 18/00842/FULM.
 
The
Development Management Lead introduced the report and informed
members that an update sheet had been circulated to the
committee.  She explained that
paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 had to be amended as the information was
incorrect and it was not necessary to refer the application to the
Secretary of State.  The drawing numbers
had also been amended following the publication of the agenda and
report.
 
There
were no questions from the committee for the officer.  The Chair invited Laurence Moore to speak to the
committee on behalf of the applicant.
 
Laurence Moore thanked the officer for her presentation which
had covered many points he had been going to mention.  He explained that mostly the amendments related to
internal aspects of the development, including an amenity suite for
residents’ use and a second stairwell to building A2, which
improved safety for residents.  
The development met the need for housing in the area.  He added that there were no material changes to
the previous conclusions.  The building
would also meet the new Building Regulation requirements for taller
buildings.  The proposal would continue
to provide a high quality development
for residents.  There was no proposal to
change the height of the buildings. 
There were significant merits in the scheme and it met the housing needs of the
borough.
 
The
Chair invited comments or questions from the committee. 
 
Councillor Bell commented that this was one of the most changed
roads in West Watford.  He accepted that
this application had not quested any material changes.  He noted the amenity space for residents and
sought assurance that it would not be available as a commercial
space.  He welcomed the inclusion of the
second stairwell and was not covered that this would require the
reduction of six flats.  However, he did
comment that residents in the existing houses were concerned about
the loss of some of the tree cover.
 
The
Development Management Lead responded to Councillor Bell’s
points.  She advised that the amenity
space would be approved as part of the residential
development.  A planning application
would be required if it was to be let externally.  The location of the space within the development
made it clear it was for residents’ use.  She then referred to the landscaping.  She explained that this was always indicative in
an application.   There was
difficulty in the location of some trees due to underground
services.  The key point was the quality
of the site for residents on the site and those surrounding
it.  Discussions would take place with
the applicant and officers would make sure trees were in
place.
 
The
Chair agreed with Councillor Bell about the need for the second
stairwell.    He acknowledged
concerns about the tree planting, but officers would keep
watch.  The amenity space was an
improvement. 
 
The
Chair invited the committee to vote on the officer’s
recommendation subject to the amendments outlined on the update
sheet.
 
On
being put to committee the application was approved as
amended.

and maintenance programme and copies of any waste transfer notes
relating to exported and imported soils shall be submitted to the
Local Planning Authority for approval. The approved monitoring and
maintenance programme shall be implemented.
 

4.         Contamination
Found (was 5)

 

           
In the event that contamination is found
at any time when carrying out the approved development that was not
previously identified it must be reported in writing immediately to
the Local Planning Authority. An investigation and risk assessment
must be undertaken, and where remediation is necessary a
remediation scheme must be prepared, which is subject to the
approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority. Following
completion of measures identified in the approved remediation
scheme a verification report must be prepared, which is subject to
the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.

 

5.         Surface Water
Drainage – Residential (was 6A)

 

           
The detailed surface water drainage scheme for the residential
section of the site shall be fully implemented in accordance with
the details approved in respect of discharge of condition
application reference 21/01516/DISCON as detailed below, unless
otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The
approved details in respect of original condition 6A are: Drainage Statement (prepared by GTA, ref:
965489, dated: 29.09.2021) Site Drainage Plan (ref: 10493/1601,
rev: P3, dated: 29.09.2021) Site Drainage Details (Sheet 1 and 2,
ref: 10493/1701 and 10493/1702, dated: 15.05.2020)

 

6.         Surface Water
Drainage – Commercial (was 6B)

 

           
Other than demolition and site investigation works, no commercial
development approved by this planning permission shall take place
until a detailed surface water drainage scheme for the commercial
section of the site has been submitted to, and approved in writing,
by the local planning authority. The surface water drainage system
will be based on the submitted Flood Risk Assessment & Drainage
Strategy, Version 1, SLR Ref:402.07391.00004, dated June 2018,
produced by SLR and all supporting information. The details should
include:

           
1. Specification of the agreed discharge rate with Thames Water and
clarification for which return period.

           
2. Specification of the proposed discharge total rate for the site
for the 1 in 1 year, 1 in 30 years, 1 in 100 years and 1 in 100
yeas + 40% for climate change allowance.

           
3. Specification of the proposed discharge rates for each of the
proposed sites, that is, Blocks A & B, Warehouse and Terraced
House.

           
4. Providing attenuation to ensure no increase in surface water
run-off volumes for all rainfall events up to and including the 1
in 100 year + 40% climate change event
for the entire site.

           
5. Implementing the appropriate drainage strategy based on
attenuation and discharge into Thames Water surface water sewer
network using appropriate SuDS
measures, like permeable pavement below ground crates as indicated
on the drainage strategy.

           
6. Detailed engineered drawings of the proposed SuDS features and discharge control devices
including their, location, size, volume, depth and any inlet and
outlet features.

           
7. Detailed surface water calculations and modelling and respective
attenuation volumes for all rainfall events up to and including the
1 in 100 year + climate change event
supported by a clearly labelled drainage layout plan showing pipe
networks.

           
8. Detailed design of the drainage scheme layout including detailed
engineered drawings of the proposed SuDS features including their, location, size,
volume, depth and any inlet and outlet features including any
connecting pipe runs and all corresponding discharge and volume
calculations/modelling. The plan should show any pipe 'node
numbers' that have been referred to in network calculations and it should also show invert and
cover levels of manholes.

           
9. Final detailed management plan to include arrangements for
adoption and any other arrangements to secure the operation of the
scheme throughout its lifetime.

           
10. The scheme shall be fully implemented and subsequently
maintained, in accordance with the timing / phasing arrangements
embodied within the scheme, or within any other period as may
subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the local planning
authority.

 

7.         Piling for
Commercial (was 7)

 

           
No piling within the curtilage of the commercial building shall
take place until a piling method statement for the land within the
curtilage of the commercial building (detailing the depth and type
of piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling
will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the
potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the
programme for the works) has been submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority in consultation with Thames
Water. Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms
of the approved piling method statement.
 

8.         Materials
Residential (was 8)

 

           
No external facing materials shall be installed on any residential
building of the development until full details and samples of all
the materials to be used for the external surfaces of the
residential buildings have been submitted to and approved in
writing by the Local Planning Authority.

 

9.         Materials
Commercial (was 9)

 

           
The external surfaces of the commercial building shall be finished
in the materials as set out in the details of drawing WD_13-005 Rev
C4 approved pursuant to the discharge of condition application
reference 20/00526/DISCON unless otherwise approved in writing by
the Local Planning Authority.

 

10.       Hard Landscaping
Residential (was 10)

 

           
No dwelling within the development shall be occupied until a
detailed hard landscaping scheme for the residential section of the
site, including details of the roof gardens, hardstanding, site
boundary treatments, children's play area and external lighting has
been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority, and the works have been carried out in accordance with
the approved details.

 

11.       Soft Landscaping
Residential (was 11)

 

           
No dwelling within the development shall be occupied until a
detailed soft landscaping scheme for the residential section of
site, including details of the roof gardens and appropriate
irrigation systems, and a landscape management and maintenance
plan, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local
Planning Authority. The detailed scheme shall be based upon the
Drawing No. 10911-PL_005 Rev D (Proposed Landscape Plan). The
approved soft landscaping scheme shall be carried out not later
than the first available planting and seeding season after
completion of development. Any trees or plants whether new or
existing which within a period of five years die, are removed or
become seriously damaged or diseased shall be replaced in the next
planting season with others of similar size and species, or in
accordance with details approved by the Local Planning
Authority.

 

12.       Hard Landscaping
Commercial (was 12)

 

           
The hard landscaping in respect of the commercial building shall be
finished as set out in the details of drawing WD_10-001 Rev P2
approved pursuant to the discharge of condition application
reference 20/00526/DISCON unless otherwise approved in writing by
the Local Planning Authority.

 

13.       Access (was 13)

 

           
No dwelling within the development shall be occupied until the new
access and egress arrangements from Sydney Road, as shown in
principle on the approved drawings has been completed in
full.

 

14.       Visibility Splay (was
14)

 

           
Prior to the first residential occupation of the development hereby
permitted, vehicular visibility splays measuring 25m x 2.4 metres
minimum shall be provided to each side of the new access where it
meets the highway of Sydney Road and such splays shall thereafter
be maintained at all times free from any
obstruction between 600mm and 2m above the level of the adjacent
highway carriageway.

 

15.       Bins and Bikes (was
15)

 

           
No dwelling within the development shall be occupied until the bin
and bicycle storage has been provided for the use of residents, in
accordance with the approved drawings. These facilities shall be
retained at all times for the use of the
residential occupiers of the dwellings.

 

16.       Aerials and Satellites
(was 16)

 

           
No dwelling shall be occupied until details of a communal
terrestrial television aerial(s) and satellite dish(es) have been
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The approved details shall be installed in
full.

 

17.       Car Parking Allocation
(was 17)

 

           
No dwelling shall be occupied until the details of car parking
allocation have been submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning. The provision shall include an agreed allocation of
on-site residential car parking spaces for use by the affordable
housing units. The car parking spaces shall remain available for
use by the allocated residents, in accordable with the agreed
allocations, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local
Planning Authority
 

18.       Built Drawings for
Drainage – Residential (was 18a)

           

           
Upon completion of the residential section of the site, a complete
set of as built drawings for both site
drainage and any exceedance flow route shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme
shall also include:

 

           
1. Provision of complete set of as built
drawings for the site drainage and informal flooding arrangements
shown on a plan.

           
2. Details of any inspection and sign-off requirements for
completed elements of the drainage system.

 

19.       Built Drawings for
Drainage – Commercial (was 18b)

 

           
Upon completion of the commercial section of the site, a complete
set of as built drawings for both site
drainage and any exceedance flow route shall be submitted to and
approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme
shall also include:

 

           
1. Provision of complete set of as built
drawings for the site drainage and informal flooding arrangements
shown on a plan.

           
2. Details of any inspection and sign-off requirements for
completed elements of the drainage system.

 

20.       Drainage Management
– Residential (was 19a)

 

           
Upon completion of the drainage works for the residential section
of the site, a management and maintenance plan for the SuDS features and drainage network shall be
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The scheme shall include maintenance and operational
activities and arrangements for adoption.
 

21.       Drainage Management
– Commercial (was 19b)

 

           
Upon completion of the drainage works for the commercial section of
the site, a management and maintenance plan for the SuDS features and drainage network shall be
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority. The scheme shall include maintenance and operational
activities and arrangements for adoption.

 

22.       Internal Noise (was
20)

 

           
All residential units shall achieve the recommended maximum
internal noise levels under BS 8233 through the provision of a good
quality window units with a Rw of at
least 26 dB in accordance with the noise assessment dated November
2017 prepared by SLR (Ref 402.07391.00002).

 

23.       Commercial Use (was
21)

 

           
The commercial premises shall be used only as for uses within
Classes E (g)(iii) and B8 and shall be used for no other purpose
unless otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority.

 

24.       No Communications
Development (was 22)

 

           
For the avoidance of doubt, no communications development permitted
by Class B or Class C of Part 16 of Schedule 2 of the Town and
Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order
2015 shall be undertaken on the building.
 

25.       Piling (was 23)

 

           
Piling for the residential development shall be only in accordance
with the details of the document '29-43 Sydney Road, Watford,
Piling Risk Assessment, SLR Ref: 402.10903.00001 Version No: 2,
November 2021, prepared by SLR Consulting Limited', approved under
discharge of condition reference 21/01640/DISCON dated 27.01.2022,
unless otherwise approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority.

 

26.       Water Use

 

           
The residential development hereby approved shall not be occupied
until details have been submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority to confirm that the dwellings have been
completed to meet the water efficiency optional requirement of 110
litres of water per person per day.

 

27.       Part M
Compliance

 

           
The residential development hereby approved shall not be occupied
until details have been submitted to and approved in writing by the
Local Planning Authority to confirm that all but the identified 33
of the dwellings hereby approved have been built to the Building
Regulations (2010) Access to and use of Buildings, Approved
Document M (2015 as amended), Volume 1: Dwellings, M4 (2):
Accessible and adaptable dwellings. The dwellings not required to
be included in this condition are as follows:

           
o Block A1, units A1-3-01, A1-3-02, A1-4-01, A1-4-04, A1-6-01 and
A1-6-02;

           
o Block A2, units A2-1-02, A2-1-03, A2-1-04, A2-8-01, A2-8-08,
A2-10-01, A2-10-02, A2-10- 03 and A2-10-04;

           
o Block B, Units B-1-01, Unit B-1-02, Unit B-1-03, Unit B-1-04,
Unit B-1-05, Unit B-1-06, Unit B-1-07 and Unit B-1-08;
and

           
o Block C, Units C-1-01, C-1-02, C-1-03, C-1-04, C-1-05, C-1-06,
C-1-07, C-1-09, C-5-04 and C5-05.

 

28.       EV Charging

 

           
Of the car parking spaces approved, a minimum of 20% shall be
installed with active charging infrastructure for electric
vehicles. All other spaces shall be installed to include passive
provision for electric vehicle charging.

 

Informatives

 
           
IN912 Hours of Construction
           
IN913 Community Infrastructure Levy Liability
           
IN914 Section 106 Undertaking
           
IN909 Street Naming and Numbering
           
IN907 Consideration of proposal in a positive and proactive
manner
           
IN915 Highway Works – HCC agreement required

content:
Application
Ref No: 23/01535/PREMV
Date of
hearing: 2 December 2025
 
Sub-committee members: [Chair]:           
Councillor Amanda Grimston
                       
                                               
Councillor Asma Suleman
                       
                                               
Councillor Sam Summer
 
Officers:         Kerrie
Marks, Community Protection, Service Delivery Lead
           
           
Kevin Chin, Licensing and Compliance Manager
           
           
Kerry Musgrave, Lawyer (Employed Barrister)
           
           
Laura MacMillan, Democratic Services Officer

           

1.              
This was an application for a variation of a premises licence in respect
of:  Vue
Cinema, Woodside
Leisure Park, Watford WD25 7JZ
 
2.         The
Sub-committee heard oral evidence from the following
witnesses:

 
1.    
Tony Jackson – Objector and local
resident

2.    
Roger Osborn – Objector and local
resident

3.    
Tim Williams – Objector and local
resident

4.    
Jonathan Smith – Applicant’s
Solicitor

5.    
Steve Wallace – Applicant

6.    
Elizabeth Morris – Applicant
           

3.         The
following persons were also present but took no part in the
Hearing:
 

1.    
none
                                   

4.         The
Sub-committee also took into account the
representations from the following in their absence:
           


1.    
Interested Parties as indicated in the
report.

 
5.         The
following representation was withdrawn prior to the
Hearing:
 
           
           
None
 

6.         The
Sub-committee took into account the
following provisions of the Licensing Act 2003:
 
           
Sections:       
Section 4
                                   
Section 18
                                   
Sections 34 and 35 (variation of a premises
licence)

                                  
The Licensing Act 2003 (Hearing) Regulations 2005 (as
amended)
 

Reasons:   These
were the relevant sections of the Act for this
application.
 

7.         The
Sub-committee took into account the
following provisions of the Secretary of State’s guidance
under section 182 of the Act (February 2025):
 

Paragraphs: 
Paragraph 2.1 – 2.4 (The Licensing
Objectives)                          
Paragraph 2.15 – 2.21 (The Prevention of Public Nuisance)
           
Paragraph 9.37 – 9.44 (Determining Applications and Imposing
Conditions)

                       
Paragraph 14.64 – 14.71 (Licensing Hours)

 

Reasons:        These were the
relevant paragraphs of the Secretary of State’s guidance for
this application.

 

8.         The
Sub-committee took into account the
following provisions of its statement of licensing
policy:
 

Paragraphs:  Policy LP6
– Prevention of Crime and Disorder              
Policy LP7 – Public Safety

                       
Policy LP8 – Prevention of public nuisance

 

Reasons:       These were the
relevant policies of the Licensing Authority’s Statement of
Licensing Policy.

 

9.         The
Sub-committee did not depart from the guidance under section 182 of
the Act. 

 

10.      The Sub-committee did not
make an exception to its statement of licensing policy.  

 

11.      The Sub-Committee has
resolved to grant the application.
 

Licensing Objectives Considered
The
Sub-Committee determined that all four licensing objectives were
relevant to this application:

Prevention of crime and disorder
Prevention of public nuisance
Public
safety
Protection of children from harm

 

Representations Reviewed
The
Sub-Committee considered all written representations and heard oral
submissions from:
 

Tony
Jackson, Roger Osborn and Tim Williams – Objectors and
local residents
Applicant’s Solicitor – Jonathan Smith, Vue Area
Managers Steve Wallace and Elizabeth Morris

 

Sub-Committee Findings
Whilst
the residents’ concerns were noted and understood, there was
no evidence that the existing licensing arrangements had
caused any problems and without clear evidence that cinema goers
were a problem, it was difficult to let those views prevail over
the licensing objectives.  It was noted
that there had been no objections or observations from the
responsible bodes. Moreover, there was no evidence that the
proposed extension would in itself
create new or additional problems.
 
Members
also noted that here may be a possibility of the extended hours
bringing some employment to the area. 
 
The
committee was keen to support and foster residents’
consultations and were pleased to hear that this was going to be
offered in the future.
 

Reasoning and Legal Considerations

1.    
The application to
amend the existing conditions and redesign seating, was not objected to and the committee
unanimously allowed that part of the application.
 

2.    
The committee also
unanimously allowed the extension of hours, having heard the
submission and discussion from all parties, they were happy to
follow the proposal of an extension to 4 am and 24 hours on 20 days
per year.  The future plans for liaison with residents and
notification of days to be used for 24 hours were noted and very
much welcomed.
 
The
objective of prevention crime and disorder, public safety and
public nuisance was addressed
by:

i)               
the
existing record of the site and no representation from responsible
authorities.

ii)              
The
fact that when the cinemas had used its
extended hours until 3am or used a Temporary Event Notice for
longer hours, there had been no specific problems as far as anyone
was aware.

iii)            
Security measures on the site

iv)            
The
restriction of alcohol sales

v)              
The
apparent majority access by car rather than foot.

vi)            
The
recent refurbishment of the cinema, reducing seat
numbers.

vii)           
The
staggering of showing, so as to prevent
number leaving at same time.

viii)         
Digital reminder signs to leave
quietly.
 
The
prevention of children from harm:

i)               
Existing licensing conditions and business practices
restricting access to unaccompanied
children after certain hours.

ii)              
There
are no assertions or evidence that children are at risk and the cinema
management is proactive in engaging with local schools.
 

Advisory

·      
To have 6 monthly meeting with residents, through
local councillor.

·      
To when possible (i.e. information given by film
distributor) to inform residents 7 days
in advance of use of extended hours.
 

 

Right of Appeal

 
Under
Schedule 5 of the Licensing Act 2003, the applicant, any
responsible authority, or any person who made a relevant
representation may appeal against this decision to the
Magistrates’ Court within 21 days of receiving this written
notification.
 
 
Signed
[Chair]:          Councillor
Amanda Grimston
                                   
Councillor Asma Suleman
                                   
Councillor Sam Summer
 
Date: 2
December 2025
topline: The Licensing Sub Committee has decided to grant an application for a variation of a premises licence for Vue Cinema, including an extension of hours to 4 am and 24 hours on 20 days per year.

content:
Cabinet
received a report of the Sports and Physical Activity Manager that
set out a local framework for the development of sports and
physical activity in Watford. 
 
The Mayor invited Councillor Pattinson to
introduce the report.
 
Councillor Pattinson introduced the
report.  She stated the report built on
the successes of the previous approach. 
The framework set out a clear and evidence-based plan.  It would help more people in Watford to become
more active more often.  It recognised
the vital role sports and activities played in bringing communities
together, improving quality of life. 
There had been a wide consultation and
this had been reflected in the final draft.  She thanked those that had been involved in the
development of the plan.  The statistics
showed that 24% of residents were inactive, which was higher in
less affluent areas, older adults, those with a disability and some
ethnic groups.
 
Councillor Pattinson said that the benefits to
residents were clear.  Regular activity
improved long term health, reducing pressures on other services and
strengthened community connections.   It helped all sections of the community in
varying ways.  It would make the most of
the town’s parks and community facilities.  It would make a real difference; it was ambitious,
inclusive, rooted in partnership and improving the health of
Watford’s residents.
 
Councillor Pattinson thanked the Sports and
Physical Activity Manager for her dedication, commitment and
passion for ensuring Watford residents could access high quality
activity that changed people’s lives and ensuring it was
accessible to all.  Councillor Pattinson
recommended the report for approval.
 
The Mayor echoed Councillor Pattinson’s
thanks to the officers concerned.  He
invited other members to comment.
 
Councillor Stotesbury welcomed the
document.  It was excellent in that it
linked to the council’s Greenspaces Strategy and Sustainable
transport initiatives.  By implementing
the framework it would change
people’s lives and make the town more
sustainable.
 
Councillor Bell thanked the Sports and Physical
Activity Manager and other officers for their work.  He mentioned an example on page 36 of the pack
referencing areas of deprivation and hoped this would be followed
through and linked to the council’s work.  He welcomed the work with the County Council and
other groups including Sport England.
 
The Mayor responded that there had been internal
discussions about those areas where there could be a particular
need.
 
Councillor Pattinson commented that it was
important to note that the framework would be insight led and data
driven.  Making sport accessible to all
was really important and the framework
could deliver that.
 
The Mayor referred to the map in the document and
how the sports activities were spread out across the
town.
 
Councillor Begum said it was an amazing
document.  She said that there was one
thing she wanted to draw out that resonated with her.  The report talked about the growing Asian
community and inequalities.  The
graphics in the document demonstrated multi-culturalism, portraying
different ethnic clothing, different people of colour, showing the
beauty of Watford’s multi-culturalism and
diversity.  She wanted to acknowledge
the inclusivity in the programme.
 
The Mayor invited Cabinet to vote on the
recommendation.
 
Resolved –
 
That
the Sports and Physical Activity Framework 2025-29 is
approved.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Sports and Physical Activity Framework 2025-29 in Watford, aiming to improve community health and well-being through sports and physical activities.

content:
Cabinet
received a report of the Chief Finance Officer and the minutes from
Finance Scrutiny Committee held on 18 September 2025.  The report set out the latest financial position
as at Quarter 1 of 2025/26. 
 
The Mayor invited Councillor Begum to introduce
the report.
 
Councillor Begum informed members that the report
was the first of the financial year and focused on the year end
position compared to the original budget approved at Council on 28
January 2025.  She advised that the
report had also been presented to Finance Scrutiny Committee at its
meeting on 18 September 2025.  She had
been pleased to receive some positive feedback.  The report highlighted some positive trends and further information would be shared with
Finance Scrutiny Committee following the members’
request.  She referred to the General
Fund reserves and advised that as at 30
June these remained at the risk assessed level of £2
million.  She confirmed that the reserve
would increase to circa £4 million once work had been
completed.  She recommended the report
to Cabinet.
 
The Mayor invited Councillor Pattinson to
speak.
 
Councillor Pattinson wished to highlight the
positive performance of the Housing team.  The housing crisis continued, but with the
intervention and proactive work of the team the temporary
accommodation levels were beginning to fall.
 
The Mayor echoed Councillor Pattinson’s
comments about the housing work.  He
invited Cabinet to vote on the recommendations.
 
Resolved –
 

1.          that the Financial Monitoring Report 2025/26
– Quarter 1 is noted.

 

2.         that the
Revenue Virements, as set out in Appendix 7 of the report, are
recommended to Council for approval.

 

3.         that the
use of commuted sums totalling £1.650m in the capital budget
for affordable housing to support the delivery for new affordable
housing, allowing a timely response when opportunities arise,
helping to reduce pressures on temporary accommodation is
recommended to Council for approval.

 

4.         that a
net budget increase of £0.326m in the capital programme for
Corporate Asset Management WBC Properties, which will be mitigated
in part by expected additional funding from occupiers, is
recommended to Council for approval.

 

5.         that
Cabinet recommends to Council that the Chief Finance Officer is
granted delegated authority to vire
funds, realigning expenditure and income across budgets within the
budget envelope.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve financial recommendations for the first quarter of the 2025/26 fiscal year, including revenue virements and budget increases for affordable housing and corporate asset management.

content:
Cabinet
received a report of the Delivery Support Lead, which was reviewed
by Cabinet quarterly and Audit Committee twice yearly. 
 
The Mayor invited Councillor Begum to introduce
the report.
 
Councillor Begum began by thanking the Associate
Director of Customer and Corporate Services for the all the work he
did.  She informed Cabinet that this was
the first report presented to Cabinet on the refreshed
framework.  The template promoted
transparency.  It reflected the number
of strategic risks and the mitigating actions for each.  She recommended the report to
Cabinet.
 
Councillor Pattinson noted that this was the
first time the risks had been presented in this format.  She asked whether, in the next report, an
indicator could be included to show where a risk had increased or
fallen.
 
The Associate Director of Customer and Corporate
Services confirmed that this was the plan.  This report set the baseline.
 
Councillor Bell thanked the officer for the
report, but queried the ‘inherent risks’ which were
shown in red.
 
The Mayor commented that the red related to the
unmitigated risks.  The Associate
Director confirmed that this was if no action were
taken.  He advised that when a risk was
identified mitigating action was taken. 
He added that some risks were time limited and others were inherent
with the red shading in this column identifying the inherent risks
which required ongoing management.  The
report indicated that risks existed but were
managed.
 
The Mayor thanked everyone for their comments and
stressed it was important to be transparent.  He invited Cabinet to vote on the
recommendations.
 
Resolved –
 

1.         that the
updates on the actions identified in the Strategy under
‘Continuous Improvement and Future Development’ at
paragraph 4.2.7 are noted.

 

2.         that,
subject to the above, the proposed amendments to the Corporate Risk
Register for submission to Audit Committee are approved.

 

3.         that, going
forward, the updated risk register serves as the new baseline
position for managing corporate risks is noted. In line with the
risk management process, all risks will be reviewed and any changes
to risks and risk scores will be presented in the next reporting
period, scheduled for March 2026.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve proposed amendments to the Corporate Risk Register for submission to Audit Committee.

purpose:
A summary of complaints across the council in
2024/25 financial year
content:
Cabinet
received a report of the Monitoring Officer, which provided the
Annual Complaints report for 2024/25.
 
The
Mayor invited the Associate Director of Customer and Corporate
Services to introduce the report.
 
The
Associate Director informed members that the annual report was a
requirement of the Local Government and Social Care
Ombudsman.  However, he noted that the
council had produced an annual report prior to the
Ombudsman’s requirement.  The low
level of complaints was good, particularly when it was considered
against the overall number of contacts to the council.  The majority of
complaints had been responded to within the 10 days
deadline.  There were some cases that
took longer due to their complexity.  In
these cases, the customer was contacted with an explanation for any
delay.  It was important to recognise
when something did not go right.  The
process helped to identify issues and lessons were
learnt.
 
The
Mayor commented that it was helpful to see the annual
report.  He noted that last year the
Ombudsman’s letter had reported that during 2023/24 there had
been no complaints upheld.  It would be
very difficult to maintain that level.
 
Councillor Stotesbury said that he had not been surprised to see
that Housing had received the most
number of complaints, as it was one of the busiest
services.  Capturing complaints was an
important function and then learning lessons.  He asked whether, in the preparations for Local
Government Reorganisation, there was a piece of work planned for the future to capture this
information.
 
The
Associate Director responded that there was a lot of work
as a result of local government
reform.  Once the democratic process had
been completed this week officers would begin to look at transition
and what that meant for the future.
 
The
Mayor added that from his perspective it was necessary to focus on
best practice across the county, sharing information.  Also, part of best practice was to learn from the
complaints and reviewing processes.
 
The
Chief Executive advised that officers were in the process of
starting to scope what the next stage would look like, a transition
plan.  There would definitely be one stream focusing on customer
services.
 
Councillor Bell stated that it was important to learn from
complaints.  He asked about officer
training.
 
The
Mayor acknowledged there was a lot of training.  The Chief Executive added that any comments from
the Local Government Ombudsman were reviewed and consideration given to do things
better.
 
Councillor Pattinson commented that the Housing team were
currently updating policies, for example the Housing Nominations
Policy.  Information received through
complaints was reviewed and then the lessons learnt built into the
policies and procedures.
 
As
there were no further questions or comments, the Mayor invited
Cabinet to vote on the recommendations.
                       
Resolved –

 

1.         that the
Annual Complaints Report 2024/25 is approved.

 

2.         that the LGSCO
Annual Letter 2024/25 is noted.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Annual Complaints Report for 2024/25.

content:
Cabinet
received a report of the Safeguarding Manager, which provided an
updated Safeguarding Children, Young People and Adults at Risk
Policy and procedures.
 
The
Mayor invited Councillor Dychton to introduce the
report.
 
Councillor Dychton began by stating that safeguarding was at the
heart of the council’s work; protecting those who may be
vulnerable.  The updated policy would
strengthen the council’s commitment to deliver a safe and
legally compliant practice across the council.  She informed members that the policy had last been
reviewed in 2021.  However, safeguarding
guidance had evolved since then.  She
wished to acknowledge the excellent work which had been led by the
Safeguarding Manager.  There was a
clearer procedure, improved consistency in practice and a stronger
network of safeguarding officers, and an improved representation of
front-line services.  She stressed that
training and awareness were essential. 
A refreshed training plan had been developed for officers and
members, ensuring all understood their responsibility and providing
confidence in recognising concerns.  It
was not a role for a single team, but sharing responsibility across
the organisation.
 
Councillor Dychton added that the policy reflected the
council’s wider community safety ambitions and supporting
vulnerable people.  The updated policy
ensured the council remained up to date, compliant and more
importantly protecting residents.  She
recommended the report to Cabinet.
 
Councillor Bell commended the report and the policy and
procedures.  He noted many of the
policies were linked to the County Council.  It was important that it was reviewed and
updated.  He considered that all members
should read through the documents.
 
The
Mayor asked about training for councillors.
 
The
Safeguarding Manager explained that she was working with the
Democratic Services Lead to find a date in the new year for member
training.  However, if anyone wanted a
specific area covered to let her know. 
She added that members would also be welcome to attend the staff
training sessions, but noted these would be during the
day.
 
The
Mayor thanked the officer and invited Cabinet to vote on the
recommendation contained in the report.
 
Resolved –

 
That
the updated Safeguarding Children, Young People and Adults at Risk
Policy and Procedures are approved.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the updated Safeguarding Children, Young People and Adults at Risk Policy and Procedures.

grant the application for the variation of the Premises Licence in

responsible authority.

Considered

four licensing objectives were relevant to this
application:

·               
Prevention
of crime and disorder

·               
Prevention
of public nuisance

·               
Public
safety

·               
Protection
of children from harm

Reviewed

from:

Ms. Kamila
De Sa Teles and Ms. Cynthia – Objectors and local

·               
Applicant’s
Solicitor - George Domleo, Applicant -Timothy Halpin, and

·               
Ms.
Letitia Jackson – Police Licensing Officer

regarding crime and disorder, public nuisance, anti-social
behaviour, and public safety. They reported incidents of patrons
behaving aggressively outside the premises, urinating in the
street, broken glass found nearby, and noise levels that disrupted
their enjoyment of their homes during weekends.

Hertfordshire Constabulary, supported the application. She
confirmed that the premises had previously operated under eight
Temporary Event Notices (TENs) replicating the hours sought in the
variation application. These events were well managed, and no
complaints were received. One incident occurred outside the
premises during the last event on 25 October 2025, which was
promptly reported and appropriately handled. Police raised no
concerns regarding the management of the
premises.

 

The Applicant’s Solicitor
stated that the premises are part of the Star Pubs Group, which
operates in over 38 cities. The premises is well managed, as
confirmed by the Police, and no Responsible Authority objected to
the application. The successful operation of previous TENs
demonstrated that the premises is a responsible operator committed
to working with residents. In addition to agreed conditions, it was
discussed with the Designated Premises Supervisor that an
additional condition may be agreed: no entry after 22:00
hours. They also agreed to provide the Designated Premises
Supervisor’s (DPS) telephone number and email address to
residents.

 

Sub-Committee
Findings

The Sub-Committee concluded that the
premises is well run and compliant with existing licence conditions
and licensing objectives. In determining the application, the
Sub-Committee was mindful of its duty to ensure, on the balance of
probabilities, that granting the variation would safeguard and
promote the licensing objectives.

The Sub-Committee therefore grants
the application to vary the Premises Licence, subject
to:

·               
All
conditions proposed and agreed with Responsible
Authorities

 

Reasoning and Legal
Considerations

The Sub-Committee is satisfied that
this variation will allow the business to continue operating while
ensuring that the licensing objectives are not
undermined.

 

In reaching its decision, the
Sub-Committee had due regard to:

 

·               
The
Licensing Act 2003

·               
The
licensing objectives

·               
Section
182 Guidance

·               
The
Council’s Statement of Licensing Policy

·               
The Human
Rights Act 1998

·               
The public
sector equality duty under section 149 of the Equality Act
2010

The Sub-Committee confirms that it
has fulfilled its duties under the Equality Act 2010 and considered
all written and oral evidence presented.

 

Advisory

The Sub-Committee encourages the
Applicant to:

·               
Provide
the DPS’s telephone number and email address to residents
upon request.

·               
Ensure
full compliance with all conditions attached to the Premises
Licence.

 
 
 
Right of Appeal
 
Under Schedule 5 of the Licensing Act 2003, the
applicant, any responsible authority, or any person who made a
relevant representation may appeal against this decision to the
Magistrates’ Court within 21 days of receiving this written
notification.

Saffery

licence for Café Cidade Ltd of 83B Whippendell Road,
Watford, WD18 7NH.

 

         The
Sub-committee found that all four licensing objectives, prevention
of crime and disorder, the prevention of public nuisance,
prevention of public safety and protection of children from harm
were relevant to this application. 

 

         The
Sub-committee reviewed all written representations received,
including those both supporting and opposing the application. Oral
submissions were heard from:

 

         Mrs
Bharti Patel (objector and representative local resident),
Karine Meira and Mickelli Denise Preto (the Applicants) and
Manuel Rocha (the Applicant’s Representative), Letitia
Jackson (Police Licensing Officer)

 

         Mrs
Patel raised concerns relating to crime and disorder, public
nuisance, and the protection of children from harm. She stated she
had video evidence showing vehicles obstructing waste collection
near her property, incidents of fly-tipping, loud music, shouting,
smoking, and littering. She also alleged that the premises
regularly operated beyond its licensed hours.

 

         Ms
Jackson, representing Hertfordshire Constabulary, provided evidence
of repeated breaches of licence conditions, including complaints of
noise and anti-social behaviour. She confirmed that the Police are
investigating an allegation of racial abuse linked to the premises.
Enforcement visits have been conducted, and warnings issued. On 9
October 2025 at 8:30pm, Police officers found the premises open in
breach of its licensed hours. A staff member incorrectly stated
that the premises was permitted to be open and sell alcohol until
10pm.

 

         The
Sub-committee concluded that the premises must demonstrate
compliance with existing licence conditions and ensure staff are
adequately trained to uphold the licensing objectives. The evidence
presented indicated that the premises had not consistently operated
in accordance with its licence.

 

         In
determining the application, the Sub-committee was mindful that the
concern here is to be confident on the balance of probabilities
that the licensing objective of the prevention of crime and
disorder, protection of children from harm, the prevention of
public nuisance, and public safety will be safeguarded and promoted
if the application was granted.

Sub-committee has resolved to grant a partial amendment to the
application by permitting the premises to open from
7:00am.  The remainder of the
application is refused.

 

         The
Sub-committee is satisfied that this limited variation will allow
the business to continue operating while ensuring that the
licensing objectives are not undermined, provided that all existing
conditions are strictly adhered to.  

 

         In
reaching its decision, the Sub-committee had due regard to and
considered any implications that may arise from the Human Rights
Act 1998, its public sector equality duty under section 149 of the
Equality Act 2010 and considered that in reaching the decision

2010.

 

         In
reaching its decision the Sub-committee had due regard for all that
the members had read, seen, and heard. They took into account the
provisions of Licensing Act 2003, the Licensing objectives, s182

policy.  

 

        
In reaching its decision, the Sub-committee has also had due regard
to:

·       
Article 1 Protocol 1 of the European Convention on Human
Rights (peaceful enjoyment of possessions).

·       
Article 8 (right to respect for private and family
life).

·       
Section 149 of the Equality Act 2010 (public sector
equality duty).

The decision
represents a necessary and proportionate interference with the
applicant’s rights to protect the rights and freedoms of
others and promote the licensing objectives.

 

        
Advisory: The

training records and ensure full compliance with all conditions

Cabinet received a report of the
Housing Resettlement Manager, which provided a new Housing
Nominations Policy for
adoption.
 
The
Mayor invited Councillor Pattinson to introduce the
report.
 
Councillor Pattinson stated she was pleased to introduce the
newly revised Housing Nominations Policy.  Firstly, she wished to thank the officers in the
Housing Team for their work on this important policy.  They had carried out consultation with applicants,
residents, housing associations and other stakeholders.  The policy was last updated in 2018.  She noted that many things had changed since
then.
 
Councillor Pattinson informed Cabinet that there had been 13 key
changes.  She highlighted some of the
more significant ones.  Access to the
housing register included updating the local connection rules
making them fairer and more flexible. 
The banding system had been simplified, ensuring they were clearer,
and priority was where it was most needed.  There was an update that affected those on the
single homeless pathway with access to settled
accommodation.  There were clearer rules
on offers and safeguards for care leavers moving into stable
housing.     
 
Councillor Pattinson added that as a result of the consultation,
an Exceptions Panel was to be introduced.  The panel would deal with the most complex cases,
as not every housing case fitted a set criteria. 
 
Councillor Pattinson finished by stating that the policy would
help to reduce the use of temporary accommodation, speed up
lettings and make the best use of the housing
available.  An Equalities Impact
Assessment had been completed and mostly there was a positive
impact.  However, where there were
potential negative impacts, there were mitigations in
place.   In summary she said the
revised policy would ensure the council was fairer, clearer and
more responsive to the housing challenges facing
Watford.  She recommended the policy to
Cabinet for approval.
 
The
Mayor stated that there had been lengthy internal discussions as
the policy was developed.  He was
pleased to see the introduction of the Exceptions
Panel.
 
Councillor Stotesbury noted the tough job the Housing team had
and he thanked them for their hard work, which they did with
compassion.
 
Councillor Begum noted that in the most recent first quarter
finance monitoring report, the gap regarding temporary
accommodation was beginning to close, and the trajectory was going
down.  She said this policy would help
to reinforce that.  The policy was
supported from a finance
perspective.
 
The
Mayor referred to temporary accommodation as it was a challenging
situation.  There were a number of
factors that affected people in temporary accommodation, which were
outside the control of the council.  He
asked whether this policy would help to reduce the numbers in
temporary accommodation. 
 
The
Associate Director of Housing and Wellbeing acknowledged it would
help.  However, it was important to
recognise that social housing was not the main solution for most
people.  The private sector had a
role.  This policy would help those who
were unable to access private sector housing.  It was one tool of many that the Housing team and
the council’s partners
had.
 
The
Mayor thanked everyone for their comments.  As there were no further questions, he invited
Cabinet to vote on the
recommendations.
 
Resolved
–
 

1.     
that the Nominations Policy and the proposed implementation plan
are approved for adoption.

 

2.      that the Portfolio Holder
and Associate Director of Housing and Wellbeing to delegate the
implementation date, to be no later than 1 April
2026.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a new Housing Nominations Policy in Watford, aiming to make the council fairer, clearer, and more responsive to housing challenges.

council, the governance and operating principles of the Business
Improvement District (BID).
 
It was noted that,
in accordance with the Special Urgency Procedure Rules as set out
in section 16.0 in the Access to Information: Exemption procedure
rules in the Constitution, that the Chair of Overview and Scrutiny
Committee had agreed that this item could be exempt from the
call-in procedure rules due to the timing of the BID
Ballot.
 
The Mayor
introduced the report.  He noted that a
revised version of the report had been published and circulated to
Cabinet.  The council had nine votes and
not 10 as set out in the original version of the
report.   He paid tribute to the
Business Improvement District (BID); there was an effective team in
place.  The information contained in the
report ensured the town centre’s future
viability.  There was lots of joint
working with the council, ensuring a safe and accessible town
centre.  He added that it was important
to ensure the BID was on a sound financial footing ready for when
Local Government Reform took place. 
 
The Mayor invited
the Monitoring Officer to add further
information.
 
The Monitoring
Officer advised that the report set out each organisations’
responsibilities.  The ballot opened on
12 September and would close this Thursday, 9 October.  The result should be known by the end of the
week. 
 
Councillor
Pattinson commented on the great things the BID did, ensuring
safety as you walked through the town centre.  She felt it looked great and therefore it felt
safe.  This mattered to
people.  It made the town a better
place. 
 
Councillor
Stotesbury noted that the BID Board comprised businesses from
across the town, including Clarendon Road.  It showed the BID was trying to engage with
businesses, but was also creating a draw for the
town.
 
As there were no
further questions or comments, the Mayor invited Cabinet to vote on
the recommendations.
                       
Resolved
–
 

1.      that Cabinet supports the
Watford Business Improvement District (BID) and agrees that the
proposed Business Plan 2026-2031 (Appendix 3 to the report)
meets the required regulatory
requirements.

 

2.      that the Chief Operating
Officer is authorised to vote ‘Yes’ in relation to the
council’s 9 votes as a National Non Domestic Rates (NNDR)
levy payer in the BID ballot.

 

3.      that, subject to a
‘Yes’ vote at ballot, Cabinet confirms that the
council, as the relevant local billing authority, will manage the
billing and collection of the BID levy and its transfer to the BID
Company in accordance with the BID Regulations, and will recharge
the BID Company for the collection costs of the
levy.

 

4.      that the Chief Operating
Officer is authorised to ensure that the legal arrangements are
appropriately formulated, the council will continue to hold an
Operating Agreement together with a data protection arrangement
with the BID Company.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to support the Watford Business Improvement District (BID) and approve the proposed Business Plan 2026-2031.

Cabinet received a report of the Strategic Sustainability
Manager, which set out the latest annual report of the
Environmental Strategy. 
 
The Mayor invited Councillor
Stotesbury to introduce the
report.
 
Councillor Stotesbury explained
that the council had been working on an environmental strategy for
a number of years.  This was the second
annual report to have been presented to Cabinet.  The sustainability officers collected key data to
include in the annual report.  It had
been developed internally through the Sustainability Board and
Corporate Management Board. 
 
Councillor Stotesbury provided
some of the highlights covering the four key areas covering carbon
emissions, water usage, biodiversity and waste.  The report provided information about the targets
and outcomes for the council’s direct contributions and those
for the whole of the borough.  He noted
that some works that would contribute towards the reduction of
carbon emissions had recently been completed and therefore would
not be reflected in this report. 
According to the data there had been an increase in the borough
wide emissions related to waste. It was felt this information was
erroneous and officers were working to find out more.  He advised that waste collection was an ongoing
challenge, particularly in relation to
flats.
 
Finally, Councillor Stotesbury
wished to thank the Strategic Sustainability Manager and Director
of Sustainability, Environment and Communities for all their work
and pulling together the information for the annual
report.
 
Councillor Williams commended
officers for a very readable report.  He
said that one of the areas of his responsibility was parks and open
spaces.  He noted that the results for
tree canopy exceeded the targets for 2027 and 2030.  A green spaces strategy was currently in
development and biodiversity formed a part of it.  He did remark that street trees were no longer
managed by this council, but by the county council.  He was unclear of any replacement process should a
tree be removed due to
disease.
 
Councillor Pattinson wanted to
highlight the success of the warmer homes grant.  This was particularly important during the current
cost of living
crisis.
 
Councillor Stotesbury added that
the council should be proud of its generous carbon assistance
programme.  This was beyond the scope of
most borough
councils.
 
The Mayor thanked everyone for
their comments.  He invited Cabinet to
vote on the
recommendations.
 
Resolved
–
 

1.      that the Environmental Strategy
Annual Report 2024-25 and the associated documents are
approved.

 

2.      that the approved report
is hosted on the Sustainable Watford website and is presented to
the relevant groups as described in the engagement
section.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the Environmental Strategy Annual Report 2024-25.
